newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat's Alfa Romeo set for "relaunch" in '97.
newsitem.headline: Fiat's Alfa Romeo set for "relaunch" in '97.

text.p: Fiat's upmarket car making subsidiary Alfa Romeo is set for a "relaunch" in 1997 with new engines and and new models, said Fiat Auto's managing director Roberto Testore.
Testore told an Alfa Romeo conference in this north-western Italian town that the years after 1996 will be fundamental for the relaunch of the Alfa Romeo marque.
The second half of 1997 sees the replacement for the Alfa 155, and then in the first months of 1998 sees the new 164, the largest in Alfa's range of cars.

Alfa's two other major models, the 145 and 146 will get new engines from early next year. These will see three new multi-value engines of the Twin Spark family in substitution for older Boxer engines.
With these new versions the production of there two models is expect to rise to around 105,000 from 75-80,000 currently.
For 1996, Alfa Romeo hopes to sell around 125,000 cars -- 75-80,000 of the 145 and 146, 18,000 sports cars (Spider and Gtv), 25,000 of the 155 and 6-7,000 of the 164.
